new_task_1.title: Restore coarsest pandas timestamp resolution handling in CF time unit parsing
new_task_1.description: CF time unit parsing now casts the parsed reference date timestamp to the coarsest pandas-supported resolution (`s`, `ms`, `us`, or `ns`) that preserves the same value before stripping timezone information. This compensates for changed pandas timestamp-construction behavior and restores the older xarray behavior where reference-date resolution more closely matches the precision implied by the input string rather than always remaining at nanosecond precision.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when xarray parses CF-compliant time-unit strings with textual reference dates, the resulting pandas `Timestamp` reference date uses the coarsest resolution that preserves the original value. Without this normalization, changes in pandas timestamp construction can leave parsed reference dates at unnecessarily fine resolution, which can alter inferred datetime precision during encoding and decoding.

expectation.grounded: After `_unpack_netcdf_time_units` returns the textual reference date, `_unpack_time_unit_and_ref_date` must construct a `pd.Timestamp`, cast it through `_cast_timestamp_to_coarsest_resolution`, and only then strip any timezone via `_maybe_strip_tz_from_timestamp`. The helper must try resolutions in order `s`, `ms`, `us`, `ns` and return the first unit whose `timestamp.as_unit(unit)` compares equal to the original timestamp. `_check_higher_resolution` must reuse the same ordered resolution list rather than duplicating it inline.
expectation.conceptual: Reference dates parsed from CF time-unit strings should retain only the precision they actually need. Users should observe timestamp precision that matches the input date string as closely as possible, even on pandas versions that no longer infer coarse units automatically.

constraints.grounded: The cast must not change the timestamp value; it may only reduce the stored resolution when `as_unit()` yields an equal timestamp. If no coarser representation preserves equality, the original timestamp must be kept. Existing timezone stripping behavior must remain in place after the cast.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must preserve exact datetime values while normalizing precision. It should only affect reference-date resolution inference, not unrelated time-decoding logic.

behavior: Parsing a CF units string now normalizes the reference-date `Timestamp` to the coarsest equal pandas time resolution before further processing.
A reference date such as `2000-01-01T00` can now remain at second resolution instead of being forced to nanosecond precision when pandas would otherwise preserve `ns`.
Higher-resolution reference dates that require millisecond, microsecond, or nanosecond precision retain the first resolution that exactly preserves their value.
The ordered pandas time-resolution list is centralized and reused by both reference-date casting and higher-resolution checks.
acceptance_criteria: When xarray unpacks a CF time-unit string whose reference date has whole-second precision, the returned pandas `Timestamp` should use second resolution if that preserves the value exactly.
When the reference date includes millisecond or microsecond precision, xarray should preserve the coarsest matching unit rather than always falling back to nanoseconds.
When no coarser unit exactly preserves the timestamp value, the original timestamp precision should be retained.
Parsing a reference date with timezone information should still remove the timezone after the resolution-normalization step.

new_task_2.title: Preserve lazy explicitly indexed data by avoiding `.data` access in Variable and CF coders
new_task_2.description: Several `Variable` methods and CF time encoders now use internal metadata (`._data`, `.shape`, `.dtype`) instead of materializing through `.data`. This preserves `ExplicitlyIndexed` and other lazy array wrappers during operations such as `drop_encoding`, padding, broadcasting, and datetime/timedelta encoding, avoiding unintended eager loading or coercion to NumPy arrays.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray operations which only need array metadata or a shallow data reference do not access `Variable.data`, because doing so can materialize lazy or explicitly indexed arrays and strip their specialized wrapper types. Users working with lazy backend arrays should be able to perform metadata-preserving operations such as dropping encoding, padding, broadcasting, and CF datetime/timedelta encoding without forcing eager data conversion.

expectation.grounded: In `Variable._replace`, the default data copy path must copy `self._data` rather than `self.data`. Padding helpers must derive sizes from `self.shape` rather than `self.data.shape`. The broadcast path that returns the existing data unchanged must use `self._data`. In `CFDatetimeCoder.encode` and `CFTimedeltaCoder.encode`, the dtype checks must use `variable.dtype` instead of `variable.data.dtype` before calling `unpack_for_encoding(variable)`.
expectation.conceptual: Operations that inspect or forward variable data without actually needing NumPy values should preserve the existing lazy/indexed backing object. xarray should avoid incidental realization of lazy arrays when only dtype or shape information is required.

constraints.grounded: The change must not alter the user-visible semantics of `Variable` replacement, padding widths, stat-length defaults, broadcasting, or CF encoding beyond preserving lazy wrappers. Datetime encoding must still trigger only for variables whose dtype is a `datetime64` subtype or that contain cftime datetimes, and timedelta encoding must still trigger only for `timedelta64` dtypes.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must be behavior-preserving for eager NumPy-backed variables while preventing unnecessary realization for lazy backends. Array contents, dimensions, attrs, and encoding must remain unchanged.

behavior: Methods that previously copied or forwarded `Variable.data` now preserve the original internal backing array by using `Variable._data`.
Padding logic derives sizes from `Variable.shape`, so it can compute pad widths and `stat_length` without touching the concrete array object.
Broadcasting that does not need to expand dimensions returns the existing internal array object without materializing it.
CF datetime and timedelta encoders decide whether to encode based on `variable.dtype`, avoiding premature access to `variable.data`.
A lazy or explicitly indexed array wrapper remains wrapped after metadata-only operations such as `drop_encoding()`.
acceptance_criteria: When `Variable.drop_encoding()` is called on a variable backed by an `ExplicitlyIndexed` array, the result should still be backed by an `ExplicitlyIndexed` array rather than an eagerly loaded NumPy array.
When padding logic computes default pad widths or `stat_length`, it should succeed using shape metadata without materializing lazy data.
When broadcasting a variable whose dimensions already match the requested dimensions, the returned variable should preserve the original backing array object.
When CF datetime or timedelta encoding checks a lazy-backed variable, the dtype check should not require accessing `variable.data`.
